long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Albuquerque and educated in electrical engineering and computer science at Princeton, Jeff Bezos worked in finance before leaving D.E. Shaw to start an online bookstore in 1994. He expanded Amazon across e-commerce, devices, entertainment and cloud computing, turning his founder stake into the dominant source of his self-made fortune. Bezos stepped down as chief executive in 2021 but remains executive chair and a major shareholder.

His later work extends beyond retail. Amazon identifies him as founder of Blue Origin and owner of The Washington Post, while his Earth Fund and Day One Fund support climate, homelessness and early-childhood projects. His maritime holdings form a distinctive paired commission: Forbes identifies Koru as a custom-built 417-foot sailing yacht and Abeona as its dedicated support vessel, making the connection more substantial than an isolated ownership attribution.
